Hello, recently I have taken an interest in playing mtg. I was thinking of buying the m15 toolkit. I have read all of the rules multiple times and think I could possibly build a reasonable deck for games with my friends. I was wondering what the advantages and disadvantages of buying a tool kit are for a new player. Thanks.

Tool kit gives you a lot of basic cards and a bunch of lands for building a deck, as well as a few boosters. In my experience they're nothing special, but they're good for getting started with, or for bulking up a deck.

Ok so a few things. Toolkits give you a base of cards to start building decks. They won't be the best cards available, but they will give you a good overview of the different abilities that are present in the set you are buying. There are different game modes in magic. The most commonly played version is called standard, and the cards that are legal in standard change as new sets come out. The M15 toolkit is compromised of the 2015 core set, and it will be rotating out of standard in the fall. I would not suggest buying that particular toolkit if you and your friends are playing standard. The last core set is releasing in about a week, and it will probably have a toolkit or a fat pack option. If you want a base to build from I would wait a week. The set is called Magic Origins. If you buy that set your cards will be in standard for about 1.5 years which gives you plenty of time to get use out of them.

Thanks for your reply. I was thinking of getting the origions kit. But im not looking to play as at any tournaments. I just wanted to play at a very cassual level. Are all of the cards in the box only for 2015? My friend is a returning player so I don't know if he would care. Is there a significant difference between each year? Again, thanks for your, and everybody's help.

If I remember correctly, the toolkit usually contains a set list of cards from the 2015 core set and a few random boosters. I think the last 2015 I saw had a combination of boosters from the Theros Block(Theros, Journey into Nyx, Born of the Gods) and a 2015 booster pack.

Each core set varies somewhat. They have different cards, but if you haven't played much it won't matter. All of the cards will be new to you :-).

If you want to play on a casual level only, here's a cool way to do it: Grab a bunch of friends. Pick a set, for example the new Magic: Origins set. Everyone buys six boosters each. Each player opens his six boosters, and constructs a deck from the cards in the boosters. Play against each other. You'll need to buy basic lands though, but they are dirt cheap. The professor made a video about this casual way of playing.

A toolkit is a really good way to start out. It introduces you to the mechanics of a certain set, and it also provides player guides and land. Buying singles is definitely the most 'cost effective' way of doing things, but if you don't know what you're looking for it can be a bit tough. I say go buy one, tinker around, build a deck and post it over at /v/mtgdeckbuilding you might be able to get some good suggestions on it :)

The toolkits are great for beginers. The cards aren't usually that great but that's ok, you're brand new, you just need to play. I would also suggest looking for your LGS's and going through their dollar rare box to buy some "goodies" to expand your horizons some more. I saw other people suggesting to just look up and buy singles that you want instead of buying the toolkit. I really couldn't disagree with that statement more strongly. You just need cards to get started with and playing with your buds, trying to build a deck from looking through lists online and whatnot is not the point you're at.

I can't thank everyone enough for all of the help and encouragement. I am really excited about playing. I attempted to learn in high school but everyone was really toxic and hated new comers. Thanks for all of the input.
I wouldn't get a toolkit. Those always struck me as for kids. Do you have friends you can play with?
The starter kits are awesome, if only to give you enough basic lands to start your collection. Though, you can also order basic lands in bulk on amazon or ebay.
